metadata.description: The one JSON document an epoch-1 agent handler demands back from the provider: the complete, ordered set of project outputs it was asked to produce. One call carries every declared output, so a multi-output contract never degenerates into one provider request per file, and the assistant text is never assigned to a file by position. The lifecycle matches these rows against the declared output contract before a single byte is written.

Produced outputs in the exact order the declared contract lists them. The lifecycle rejects a result whose paths differ from the contract in content, count, order or multiplicity; an empty array is representable on the wire and refused by that comparison, never silently accepted as `nothing to do`.
The project-relative, forward-slashed path exactly as the declared contract spells it. It is compared, never re-derived: the provider cannot introduce a path the operator did not declare.
The complete UTF-8 file body. The declared `non-empty file` acceptance is checked against this value before the write and against the written file afterwards.
